lessons.title: The Old Regime Slabs and Higher Exemption Limits for Senior Citizens

body.text: The old regime has fewer slabs and a much steeper climb: from 5% straight to 20% at ₹5 lakh, and 30% from ₹10 lakh. Its extra exemption for senior citizens looks generous on paper but is worth at most ₹12,500 of slab tax.

children.text: The old regime is no longer the default, but millions of Indians still use it, especially those with large home loans, high HRA claims or full Section 80C investments. Whichever regime you end up in, you need to be able to read both slab tables. This lesson covers the old regime's three tables, one for each age group, and shows exactly how much the age-based limits are really worth.

body.text: Unlike the new regime, the old regime slab rates are not written into a section of the Income-tax Act itself. They are prescribed each year in the First Schedule to the annual Finance Act. They have stayed the same for many years, but a Budget could change them at any time.

body.caption: Old Regime Slabs for Resident Individuals, Tax Year 2026-27

children.text: Read the columns carefully. Age changes only the bottom of the table. From ₹5,00,000 upwards, all three age groups pay exactly the same rates: 20% up to ₹10 lakh and 30% after that. Non-residents and HUFs use the below-60 column regardless of age.

children.text: Once income crosses ₹5,00,000, the age benefit is locked in and never grows. A 65-year-old retired professor in Bhopal with ₹18 lakh of taxable income saves exactly ₹2,500 of slab tax compared with her 45-year-old neighbour on the same income. An 82-year-old saves ₹12,500. Below ₹5 lakh the benefit barely matters for residents either, because the old regime rebate of up to ₹12,500 already takes their tax to zero.

body.title: Show me the math: slab tax at ₹18 lakh for each age group

children.text: The excess over ₹10,00,000 is ₹8,00,000, taxed at 30% for everyone: ₹2,40,000. Below 60: ₹1,12,500 + ₹2,40,000 = ₹3,52,500. Senior citizen: ₹1,10,000 + ₹2,40,000 = ₹3,50,000. Super senior citizen: ₹1,00,000 + ₹2,40,000 = ₹3,40,000. The gaps are ₹2,500 and ₹12,500, the same as at ₹5 lakh or ₹10 lakh.
When Exactly Do You Become a Senior Citizen?

You are a senior citizen for a tax year if you are resident and turn 60 at any time during that year, even on its last day. The same applies to turning 80 for super senior status. You do not have to be 60 on 1 April. So someone who turns 60 in February 2027 is a senior citizen for the whole of tax year 2026-27.

body.text: The 1 April birthday trap. Under the settled legal position, a person is treated as attaining an age on the day before their birthday. Someone born on 1 April 1967 turns 60 on 1 April 2027, but is treated as attaining 60 on 31 March 2027, which is inside tax year 2026-27. They are a senior citizen for 2026-27, a full year earlier than they might expect.

children.text: Old Slabs vs New Slabs on the Same Income

body.title: Slab Tax on the Same Total Income, Before Rebate and Cess

children.text: On identical Total Income, old regime slabs always produce more tax than new regime slabs, and the gap widens fast after ₹5 lakh. At ₹15 lakh a below-60 taxpayer pays ₹2,62,500 in slab tax under the old table versus ₹1,05,000 under the new one. Even the super senior column sits far above the new regime line. The old regime can only come out ahead when its extra deductions shrink Total Income by enough to close that gap. Working out that breakeven is the subject of our course Old Tax Regime vs New Tax Regime: Which One to Choose.

children.text: Worked Example: Ramesh, a 72-Year-Old Retiree in Tiruchirappalli

Ramesh retired from BHEL and is a resident senior citizen. In tax year 2026-27 he receives a pension of ₹6,00,000 and ₹2,46,000 of interest from the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme and bank FDs. Under the old regime he claims a ₹50,000 standard deduction on his pension, a ₹50,000 deduction for a senior citizen's interest income and ₹50,000 for his and his wife's health insurance premium.

body.caption: Ramesh's Slab Tax Under Each Regime

body.text: Ramesh's higher senior citizen exemption limit and his ₹1,00,000 of extra deductions still leave him ₹49,200 worse off under the old regime. Many retirees stay on the old regime out of habit. For a pensioner without a large home loan, the new regime's ₹4 lakh nil band and ₹12 lakh rebate usually beat the old regime's age-based limits comfortably.

body.title: Old Regime Slab Tax at ₹8.4 Lakh
body.prompt: Anita, 45, is a school principal in Jaipur. She has opted for the old regime and her Total Income after deductions is ₹8,40,000. What is her slab tax, before cess?
body.explanation: Cumulative tax at ₹5,00,000 for someone below 60 is ₹12,500. The ₹3,40,000 above that is taxed at 20%, adding ₹68,000. Slab tax is ₹80,500. Her income is above ₹5 lakh, so the old regime rebate does not apply.

body.title: The Super Senior Citizen
body.question: Savitri, 84, a resident of Varanasi on the old regime, has Total Income of ₹9,00,000. What is her slab tax, before cess?
body.explanation: A super senior citizen pays nil up to ₹5,00,000. The ₹4,00,000 between ₹5 lakh and ₹9 lakh is taxed at 20%: ₹80,000. ₹92,500 is the figure for someone below 60 (₹12,500 + ₹80,000), and ₹90,000 is the figure for a senior citizen aged 60 to 79 (₹10,000 + ₹80,000).

body.title: The Old Regime Nil Band
body.textWithBlank: Under the old regime, a resident individual aged below 60 pays no slab tax on Total Income up to ₹___.
body.explanation: The nil band is ₹2,50,000 below 60, ₹3,00,000 for senior citizens and ₹5,00,000 for super senior citizens. Non-residents and HUFs use ₹2,50,000 whatever their age.

body.title: Is Mohan a Senior Citizen Yet?
body.scenario: Mohan, a resident of Nagpur, was born on 1 April 1967. He is on the old regime and has Total Income of ₹12,00,000 in tax year 2026-27. His CA's junior prepares the computation using the below-60 slabs because "Mohan only turns 60 in April 2027, after the tax year ends."
body.prompt: Is the junior right? What slab tax should Mohan pay, and how much does the correction change it?
body.modelAnswer: The junior is wrong. A person is treated as attaining an age on the day before their birthday, so Mohan attains 60 on 31 March 2027, within tax year 2026-27. He is a senior citizen for the year. Senior citizen slab tax on ₹12,00,000 is ₹1,10,000 + 30% of ₹2,00,000 = ₹1,70,000. The junior's below-60 figure would be ₹1,12,500 + ₹60,000 = ₹1,72,500. The correction saves Mohan ₹2,500 of slab tax, plus ₹100 of cess.

cards.term: First Schedule to the Finance Act
cards.definition: The part of the annual Finance Act that prescribes the old regime slab rates for the year.
A rebate of up to ₹12,500 for resident individuals with Total Income up to ₹5,00,000, making their slab tax nil.
A person is treated as attaining an age on the day before their birthday. Relevant for anyone born on 1 April.

points: Old regime slabs are nil, 5%, 20% and 30%, with 20% starting at ₹5 lakh and 30% at ₹10 lakh
The nil band is ₹2.5 lakh below 60, ₹3 lakh for senior citizens and ₹5 lakh for super senior citizens, for residents only
Age changes only the bottom of the table, so the benefit is capped at ₹2,500 for seniors and ₹12,500 for super seniors
You count as a senior citizen for the whole tax year if you turn 60 at any point in it, and age is attained the day before your birthday
On the same Total Income, old regime slab tax is always higher than new regime slab tax; deductions have to close the gap
Many retirees with pension and interest income pay less under the new regime despite the old regime's age-based limits

body.text: Slab rates and deduction limits shown are for tax year 2026-27 and can change in any Union Budget. Figures exclude surcharge and the 4% health and education cess unless stated. This lesson is for education only and is not tax advice.
